findings.gate: VOICE CHARTER §9 — any somatic/beat phrase appearing more than 3 times per book is a defect

comparison_evidence.quote: Rule: any somatic/beat phrase appearing more than 3 times per book is a defect — including new phrases invented to replace an old one.

findings.consequence: The exact phrase 'Nobody said anything' occurs 13 times across the declared canonical scope, ch01.md through ch24.md, against the ≤3-per-book cap. The r2 repair correctly removed this chapter's second use and removed its adjacent 'That was correct', bringing that latter phrase to the cap of 3 book-wide; however, this surviving line still participates in a beat phrase more than four times over the limit. At the reveal's emotional hinge, a listener hears a cadence already used in Chapters 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 15, 19, 20, 21 and 22 rather than silence shaped specifically for Lira's line. This is a book-level gate failure, not a claim that Chapter 16 originated the tic.
findings.repair_target: Run the required book-level anti-tic pass and reduce the exact phrase to no more than three occurrences across ch01.md–ch24.md. For this chapter's contribution, vary or cut line 31 without adding another repeated silence marker and without changing Lira's fixed line, Cael's 'Yes', or the surrounding no-deflection rhythm.

concerns: Density remains close to the floor: 3,950 words, only 40 above the 3,910 lower bound and 14.1% below the 4,600 target. The chapter earns its quiet and all promised action is in scene, so this is taste/headroom rather than a defect; any later cut should be netted against an addition.

Vastin's 'The whole of the apparatus — the measure, the seat, the tier, the mark — set over all the land ... I have administered that apparatus for forty years' presses close to the connection Karis refused in Chapter 15 ('It doesn't say what the thing he made has to do with yours, or with mine, or with the thing on a station's roof'). The packet authorizes Vastin's aimed-purpose beat, no live Arbiter is named, and Karis repeats 'I'm not drawing a line', so this is not a finding. Planning should keep the two-page discipline explicit in Chapter 17.

Karis says 'A dead surveyor says a hundred lamps go out on one wire' and immediately says 'I'm not drawing a line.' Identical failure is established evidence, but 'one wire' is a shared-substrate inference spoken by the character whose rule is not to infer. It is a strong image and does not explicitly identify live Arbiters with the historical apparatus; it remains a planning/taste concern under the packet's ban on theory past the page.

Seln's 'I'd wondered, for four years, what I was keeping it from' is plausible against his series span but the exact duration is not independently fixed by a dated comparison passage in this packet. It does not contradict the supplied state, so it remains a continuity watch item rather than a finding.

'has found that her legs have opinions' is the chapter's only phrase near the no-modern-idiom boundary. It is dry and Karis-shaped, but its contemporary personification is audible in an otherwise older register. Taste only.

The closing interior deliberately uses five short standalone declaratives among longer paragraphs ('The leaf did not say that'; 'The leaf said the door was him'; the two parse sentences). The contrast works because each line sharpens omission versus intention; another repair should not add more isolated declarations.

The packet-specific 'the way X [verb]' pattern sits exactly at its cap of four, at lines 7, 13, 27 and 55. The four verbs/functions differ, so the charter's identical-construction rule is not breached, but there is no headroom.

Fight/set-piece check: there is no fight or physical action set piece in this chapter. Terrain-load-bearing choreography and the 'X removed Y's ability to Z' win test are therefore not applicable. The yard circle is a memorable emotional staging mechanism, not a combat win and should not be forced into that formula.
strengths: All seven strengths recorded at r1 survived the targeted repair. The no-deflection movement remains the chapter's load-bearing success: 'He took it now. He did not catalogue it.' and 'He did not put it beside the still place, or the cord, or the light on a hill, or the row that came out short, because those were entries and this was not an entry; this was the page the entries were written on.' The cataloguer's refusal to catalogue is still an enacted choice.

The exclusion/prevention distinction remains exact and unblurred: 'A thing that is excluded is a thing the makers forgot to make room for. A thing that is prevented is a thing the makers built the whole house to keep from being born in it.' It is sharpened by the paired declaratives 'He was not the case the machine could not parse. / He was the reason the machine had been built to parse.'

Lira and Vastin's moral exchange is untouched and still exact: 'You signed the mark at kindlings.' / 'His?' / 'No. I read it, after. I did not sign it.' / 'I would have.' / 'You would have.' Vastin names the wrong without excuse; Lira neither forgives it nor turns cruelty into virtue.

The circle remains differentiated by mechanism: Brom uses a sheet and price, Seln uses an office and the cache, Karis uses two pages and a refused line, Cleon uses presence and four ledger words, and Vastin uses a forty-year institutional sum. No secondary character borrows Cael's cadence.

Cleon's compact arc survives the scaffold repair: 'You came up.' / 'I came up.' / 'Good.' and then 'lamp, marked, work, gone'. The revised 'that was the exchange, all of it' removes the repeated closer without sanding the kindness or the man's inability to answer it.

The yard's objects continue to carry relationship and state: 'a shed on the fourth, empty'; the cup 'where a healer sat when she sat'; 'a broker's broken crate' burning; Karis's 'bound hand' on the notebook; Vastin's stick across his knees. These are not decorative inventory; they price absence, injury, labor and belonging.

The fixed close is stronger after the staging repair because the straightedge and dividers are settled before Cael speaks. The destination now arrives as one uninterrupted decision and the file stops exactly on 'I want to stand in the middle of it.'

Worldbuilding is done through mechanism and use. The system appears as a clerk counting four, a sheet designed without a column, a registry that would buy Seln's cache, marks Vastin signed at kindlings, gates and tiers Cael remembers, and a straightedge used to turn history into a road. The chapter explains purpose only after those mechanisms have acted on bodies, access, work and conscience.

The scene's non-combat set-piece quality comes from ritualized geography rather than spectacle: Lira across the brazier, Brom on the shed step, Seln facing the road, Karis asleep on the bucket, Vastin on the wall and Cleon briefly at the edge. Each position determines how that person takes the news, making the yard load-bearing for the emotional choreography even though the combat win formula is correctly not applicable.
